subject: PoC next steps — deployment mode decision & stakeholder kickoff
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya.r@healthlytics.com>, Ajay Singh <ajay.s@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + PoC options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Priya / Ajay —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Wanted to capture the options we discussed and propose a lightweight PoC plan so we can get alignment on which deployment mode makes the most sense for HealthLytics. High level summary below — please ping if I missed anything.

1) Quick deployment-mode recap (tradeoffs)
- Hosted API: fastest to start, lowest operational overhead, good for non-PHI prod traffic. Shared tenant model, Redwood-managed keys, predictable per-token billing.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale; good when you need steady qps and some isolation but not full VPC.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-controlled networking, KMS/HSM integration, full audit logs — recommended if PHI or strict compliance controls are required.

2) Proposed PoC structure (recommended starter)
- Duration: 3–4 weeks total (integration + load/latency validation + quality/regression).
- Minimum footprint for Private PoC: 2 GPU nodes (we'll propose exact SKU once we confirm token/seq profiles).
- Success criteria (draft — attached as PDF): 1) end-to-end P95 latency < 120ms for the most common 512-token paths, 2) model output meets your accuracy baseline on the labeled dev set (F1 > 0.72 for entity extraction), 3) audit/logging events captured to your SIEM, 4) connectivity and KMS key rotation verified.

3) Dependencies & asks from HealthLytics
- Confirm desired deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
- Provide list of internal stakeholders and network contact for peering (if Private).
- Share a short sample of production prompt mix and a small labeled evaluation set (we can sign an NDA if needed).

4) Next steps
- If you prefer Private, Marcus will scope the infra and send a baseline cost estimate + runbook.
- I'll prepare a short MoA and SOW draft (attached: draft-moa-healthlytics.docx) for signature so we can book reservation capacity and schedule the kickoff.

I'm looping Marcus on the thread to scope the Private-specific requirements. Can we agree on a target kickoff window next week?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0148

Subject: Re: Quick recap + PoC options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the clear summary. HealthLytics will need Private (VPC) for this initial PoC — two reasons: 1) our platform processes PHI and our security team requires customer-managed keys and peering/Audit logs, and 2) we want to validate on our networking topology before any larger commit.

Stakeholders to include on the kickoff:
- Ajay Singh, Head of Security (ajay.s@healthlytics.com)
- Sanjay Mehta, CTO (sanjay.m@healthlytics.com)
- Neha Kapoor, Platform Lead (neha.k@healthlytics.com)
- Rohan Mehta, DataOps (rohan.m@healthlytics.com)

Operational notes / questions:
- We can provision VPC peering and a transit route but will need a detailed list of ports and egress requirements (Marcus, can you include this in the runbook?).
- Can you provide a rough cost delta between Hosted and Private for a 4-week PoC (ballpark only)?
- We have an internal requirement to validate an air-gapped execution for 1 week — is that something Redwood can support in the Private packaging?

We prefer a kickoff next Tuesday (28 Jul) morning PT if that works for your team.

Thanks,
Priya
VP Product | HealthLytics
priya.r@healthlytics.com | +1 617 555 0190

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 08:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + PoC options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) — Private PoC scoping

Hi Priya / team —

Thanks — short technical responses below and a proposed minimal configuration for the Private PoC. Please find the draft success criteria attached (HealthLytics_PoC_success_criteria_v1.pdf).

Private PoC considerations (summary):
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (we can also integrate with HSM solutions; note that HSM will add ~1–2 days to setup).
- Networking: typical requirements are outbound HTTPS (443) for control plane; for VPC peering we need BGP/route table entries and ports 1024–65535 open between hosts for gRPC (if you plan to use direct internal endpoints). We'll provide a full runbook link after confirmation.
- Audit & logging: we stream audit logs to a customer-managed S3 or to your SIEM; sample CloudTrail/CloudWatch format included in the runbook.

Recommended starter config for the PoC:
- 2 GPU nodes (H100-80GB preferred if you will run long context models) OR 3x A100-40GB as an alternative.
- 1 replication controller for model failover, 30 GB ephemeral KV cache allocation per node.
- Expected throughput for this config: ~120 tok/s aggregate for TGI-style MPTs; exact numbers depend on model choice and sequence length.

Estimated ballpark cost (Private PoC, 3–4 weeks):
- Infrastructure + managed private control plane: $26k–$38k (depends on GPU SKU and reserved vs spot capacity).
- For comparison, Hosted PoC (equivalent token volume): ~$5k–$9k.

Air-gapped week: we can run an isolated validation window where control plane is limited to management IPs and we disable egress for model calls — this will require a short on-site network config and a temporary exception in our control plane ACLs. It is feasible but needs explicit sign-off and a 3–4 day prep window.

Action items from Redwood (me + Stephanie):
- I will attach the detailed runbook link and the PoC sizing worksheet.
- Stephanie to send MoA/SOW for review.

Let us know if you want us to size for H100 or A100 — we can provide an updated cost worksheet by EOD if you share expected qps and average sequence length.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
